title: Circle Geometric Relationships
description: Use circle measurements, arcs, equal radii, and tangent relationships to find missing lengths and angles with Mark, relate, solve.

questions.stem_html: A circle has circumference \(18\pi\). Its area is \(k\pi\). What is k?
questions.explanation_html: The circumference is π times the diameter, so the diameter is 18. The radius is 9. Squaring the radius gives k = 81.
questions.variation: Connect circumference, diameter, radius, and area

questions.stem_html: A circle has radius 12. The shorter arc from A to B has central angle 90°. The longer arc has length \(k\pi\). What is k?
questions.explanation_html: The longer arc spans 270° of 360°. Use that fraction of circumference \(24\pi\), giving k = \(18\).
questions.variation: Use a central angle to find arc length or its complementary arc

questions.stem_html: Angle ACB is inscribed in a circle and intercepts an arc AB of measure 118°. What is the measure of angle ACB in degrees?
questions.explanation_html: The vertex is on the circle, so the angle is half the intercepted arc: 118/2.
questions.variation: Read the intercepted arc from the angle’s vertex

questions.stem_html: Points A and B are on a circle with center O. In triangle AOB, angle OAB measures 27°. What is the measure of angle AOB in degrees?
questions.explanation_html: OA and OB are equal radii, so both base angles are 27°. Subtract their sum from 180°.
questions.variation: Use the equal radii of an isosceles triangle

questions.stem_html: A line through point P touches a circle with center O at T. The radius OT is 9 and OP is 15. What is the length of PT?
questions.explanation_html: OT is perpendicular to PT. Use OP as the hypotenuse in the right triangle. The square root of 15² − 9² is 12.
questions.variation: Apply perpendicular radii and equal tangent segments

questions.stem_html: A circle has circumference \(26\pi\). Its area is \(k\pi\). What is k?
questions.explanation_html: The circumference is π times the diameter, so the diameter is 26. The radius is 13. Squaring the radius gives k = 169.

questions.stem_html: A circle has radius 18. The shorter arc from A to B has central angle 140°. The longer arc has length \(k\pi\). What is k?
questions.explanation_html: The longer arc spans 220° of 360°. Use that fraction of circumference \(36\pi\), giving k = \(22\).
questions.variation: Use a central angle to find arc length or its complementary arc

questions.stem_html: The minor arc AB of a circle measures 134°. Point C is on that minor arc, distinct from A and B. What is the measure of angle ACB in degrees?
questions.explanation_html: Angle ACB intercepts the arc that does not contain C, which is the major arc of measure 226°. An inscribed angle measures half its intercepted arc.
questions.variation: Read the intercepted arc from the angle’s vertex

questions.stem_html: PA and PB are tangent segments from P to a circle centered at O. Radius OA is 15 and OP is 25. What is PA + PB?
questions.explanation_html: Triangle OAP is right at A, so PA = 20. Both tangents from P have that length, giving 40.
questions.variation: Apply perpendicular radii and equal tangent segments

questions.stem_html: A circle has circumference \(42\pi\). Its area is \(k\pi\). What is k?
questions.explanation_html: The circumference is π times the diameter, so the diameter is 42. The radius is 21. Squaring the radius gives k = 441.
questions.variation: Connect circumference, diameter, radius, and area

questions.stem_html: A circle has radius 9. A central angle measures \(\frac{5}{6}\pi\) radians. The intercepted arc has length \(k\pi\). What is k?
questions.explanation_html: Arc length equals radius times the angle in radians. Multiplying 9 by \(\frac{5}{6}\) gives k = \(\frac{15}{2}\).
questions.variation: Use a central angle to find arc length or its complementary arc

questions.stem_html: PA and PB are tangent segments from P to a circle centered at O. The radius is 12 and OP is 20. What is the area of quadrilateral OAPB?
questions.explanation_html: The diagonal OP splits the quadrilateral into two right triangles. Each has legs 12 and 16, because the radius meets the tangent at a right angle. Their areas sum to 192.
